headsLegs.title: Count the Legs
headsLegs.hint: Imagine they were all of the first kind. How many legs (or wheels) would be missing?
headsLegs.farm: A farm has only chickens and cows. Together they have {{heads}} heads and {{legs}} legs. How many cows are there?
headsLegs.bikes: A rental shop has only bicycles and tricycles: {{heads}} vehicles with {{legs}} wheels in total. How many tricycles are there?
headsLegs.bugs: A jar holds only beetles (6 legs) and spiders (8 legs): {{heads}} creatures with {{legs}} legs in total. How many spiders are there?

explain.farm: If all {{heads}} animals were chickens, there would be {{base}} legs. Each cow adds {{extra}} legs: ({{legs}} − {{base}}) ÷ {{extra}} = {{answer}} cows (and {{other}} chickens).
explain.bikes: If all {{heads}} vehicles were bicycles, there would be {{base}} wheels. Each tricycle adds {{extra}} wheel: ({{legs}} − {{base}}) ÷ {{extra}} = {{answer}} tricycles (and {{other}} bicycles).
explain.bugs: If all {{heads}} creatures were beetles, there would be {{base}} legs. Each spider adds {{extra}} legs: ({{legs}} − {{base}}) ÷ {{extra}} = {{answer}} spiders (and {{other}} beetles).

ages.title: Age Riddle
ages.hint: Call the younger age x and write both sentences as equations.
ages.askYounger: Mia is {{ratioNow}} times as old as her nephew Leo. In {{years}} years, she will be {{ratioLater}} times as old as him. How old is Leo now?
ages.askOlder: Mia is {{ratioNow}} times as old as her nephew Leo. In {{years}} years, she will be {{ratioLater}} times as old as him. How old is Mia now?
ages.explain: Leo is {{younger}} and Mia is {{older}} ({{ratioNow}} × {{younger}}). In {{years}} years they will be {{youngerLater}} and {{olderLater}}, and {{olderLater}} = {{ratioLater}} × {{youngerLater}}.

sumDiff.title: Sum and Difference
sumDiff.hint: If you remove the difference from the total, what is left is shared equally.
sumDiff.numbers: Two numbers add up to {{sum}}. Their difference is {{diff}}. What is the larger number?
sumDiff.shop: A notebook and a pen cost {{sum}} coins together. The notebook costs {{diff}} coins more than the pen. How many coins does the pen cost?

explain.shop: Pen = (total − difference) ÷ 2 = ({{sum}} − {{diff}}) ÷ 2 = {{answer}}. Check: the notebook costs {{large}}, and {{answer}} + {{large}} = {{sum}}.

consecutive.title: In a Row
consecutive.hint: Consecutive numbers are spread evenly around their average.
consecutive.askSmallest: The sum of {{count}} consecutive whole numbers is {{sum}}. What is the smallest of them?
consecutive.askLargest: The sum of {{count}} consecutive whole numbers is {{sum}}. What is the largest of them?
consecutive.explain: The average of the {{count}} numbers is the middle value: {{middle}}.

handshakes.title: Handshakes
handshakes.hint: With n people, each one shakes n − 1 hands, but every handshake involves two people.
handshakes.ask: At a meeting, everyone shook hands exactly once with everyone else. There were {{handshakes}} handshakes. How many people were at the meeting?
handshakes.explain: With n people there are n × (n − 1) ÷ 2 handshakes.
